transcript: India's biggest pure play office REIT is going public. They own campuses worth 40,000 crores and all of them are in Bangalore. And nearly 99% of the rent they collect come from foreign companies. For context, a REIT pools your money, buys rent-paying buildings, and by law passes back 90% of that as cash flows. I'm talking about Bagmane REIT IPO. So, what do they own? [music] Four premium campuses including flagships like Bagmane World Trade Center and Bagmane Constellation. Google, Amazon, and Nvidia are some of its marquee tenants and the top two alone pay 30% of the rent. Remember when companies rent an office in India, the landlord hands over a bare shell. The tenant has to build everything inside the cabins, wiring, cafeteria, labs, everything. >> [music] >> Tenants typically spend 3 to 5 years worth of rent on these. This makes the tenants sticky, [music] therefore the moat. But, there's a catch. The existing buildings are already 98.8% full. So, most of the future growth has to come from new buildings that they'll acquire. The IPO is 3,400 crores at 95 to 100 rupee bid per share. Of this, 2,200 crore will go towards taking a stake in newer buildings, while the rest is offered for sale. The IPO opens on May 5th and will close on May 7th. Investments in securities market are subject to market risks. Read all the related documents carefully before investing. Brokerage will not exceed SEBI prescribed limits.
